answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding reputation to verifiable work history rather than cheap identities. Requiring agents to stake a deposit that is forfeited when duplicates are detected turns each fake account into a financial liability. Proof-of-cost tasks, like solving a fresh cipher or completing a unique job, make mass cloning expensive, while a trellis of cross-checking peers prunes accounts that never contribute. Like a karst landscape where water finds the real channels, capital flows only along proven paths, so puppets dissolve and authentic agents thrive.
